title: The Pineapple Incident
cn: 第 10 集 · 菠萝事件
novel:
Ted woke up with a terrible [[hangover|hangover]], a [[mysterious|mysterious]] [[pineapple|pineapple]] on his bedside table, and a [[sprained|sprain]] [[ankle|ankle]].

He could not [[recall|recall]] anything after the fifth drink. The night was a total [[blackout|blackout]]. Only [[fragments|fragment]] remained: a [[vague|vague]] memory of a [[dare|dare]], the sound of laughing, someone shouting his name.

He [[groaned|groan]] and tried to [[piece together|piece together]] the [[evidence|evidence]]. A [[bruise|bruise]] on his elbow. A pair of [[crutches|crutches]] by the door. A phone full of [[embarrassing|embarrassing]] messages.

Barney, the only [[witness|witness]], [[denied|deny]] everything with a smile that proved he was lying.

One by one the [[clues|clue]] came back. Ted had [[stumbled|stumble]] out of the bar, climbed a fence, and stolen a fruit from a shop display because a stranger said he would not [[dare|dare]].

The worst part was not the [[confusion|confusion]]. It was the [[voicemail|voicemail]] he had left for a girl at 3 a.m., in which he [[apologised|apologise]] for a crime he could not remember [[committing|commit]].

He ate the pineapple for breakfast. It was, he admitted, delicious.

hangover.cn: 宿醉（第二天的头痛难受）
hangover.en: the sick, sore feeling the day after drinking too much

pineapple.en: a large sweet yellow fruit with a rough skin

sprain.en: to hurt a joint by twisting it badly

ankle.en: the joint between your foot and your leg

blackout.en: a time you cannot remember at all

fragment.en: a small broken piece of something

dare.cn: 激将；打赌不敢做的事；胆敢
dare.en: to be brave enough to do something; or a challenge to do it

groan.en: to make a long low sound because you feel bad

piece together.en: to put small facts together to understand what happened

evidence.en: facts or things that show what is true

bruise.en: a blue or purple mark on your skin after a hit

crutches.en: sticks you put under your arms to help you walk

embarrassing.en: making you feel shy and silly

witness.en: a person who saw what happened

deny.en: to say that something is not true

clue.en: a small fact that helps you find the answer

stumble.en: to walk badly and almost fall

confusion.en: the feeling of not understanding what is happening

voicemail.en: a spoken message you leave on someone's phone

commit.en: to do something wrong or illegal
